**Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** is a **UK Act of Parliament** dealing primarily with **tax law**. It was passed in 2010 as part of the government’s response to the **June 2010 Emergency Budget** and related fiscal changes.

## What it is
- **Jurisdiction:** United Kingdom
- **Type:** Public General Act
- **Purpose:** To implement and amend various tax measures, especially those affecting:
  - **income tax**
  - **capital gains tax**
  - **corporation tax**
  - **excise duties / duties / anti-avoidance rules**
  - other Finance Act-type tax changes

It is one of the annual “Finance Acts” through which the UK Parliament gives legal effect to budget measures.

## Historical context
In 2010, the UK had:
- the tail end of the **Labour government’s** fiscal legislation early in the year, and then
- the new **Coalition Government’s Emergency Budget** in June 2010.

The **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010** is associated mainly with the **post-election fiscal package** and urgent tax changes introduced that summer.

## Key measures commonly associated with it
Some of the most significant changes linked to this Act include:

### 1) Higher rate of income tax for top earners
- It implemented the **50% additional rate of income tax** for incomes above the relevant threshold (introduced from **6 April 2010** for the 2010–11 tax year).

### 2) Capital Gains Tax increase
- It raised the **main rate of Capital Gains Tax (CGT)** for higher-rate taxpayers from **18% to 28%** on gains above the annual exemption.
- This was a major change and one of the most publicly discussed measures.

### 3) Various anti-avoidance and technical tax changes
- Like most Finance Acts, it also contained:
  - anti-avoidance provisions,
  - amendments to existing tax rules,
  - transitional arrangements,
  - technical corrections.

### 4) Other budget-linked adjustments
Depending on the area, the Act also dealt with other fiscal and duty-related matters needed to implement budget policy.

## How it fits into UK tax law
The Act is part of the broader annual sequence of UK Finance legislation:
- **Finance Act 2010**
- **Finance (No. 2) Act 2010**
- later Finance Acts in 2011, 2012, etc.

The “**No. 2**” title means it was the **second Finance Act passed in that calendar year**.

## Legal significance
This Act mattered because it:
- changed the tax burden on high earners and investors,
- marked a shift in UK post-crisis fiscal policy,
- and became part of the modern framework for UK income tax and CGT rates.

## Practical effect
For taxpayers in 2010 onward, it meant:
- more tax for those with higher incomes,
- higher CGT on disposals above the basic rate band,
- and updated rules that tax professionals had to incorporate into planning and returns.

## If you want the exact text
The official source is the **UK legislation database**:
- **legislation.gov.uk**
- search for **“Finance (No. 2) Act 2010”**

## Caveat
Because Finance Acts are detailed and amended over time, the exact practical effect of any section may depend on:
- commencement dates,
- transitional rules,
- later amendments,
- and HMRC guidance.

If you want, I can also give you:
1. a **section-by-section summary**,  
2. the **full list of provisions**, or  
3. a **plain-English explanation of what it changed for taxpayers**.
